overview.headline: Merge sort uses divide and conquer to sort in theta n log n time

keyPoints.point: Merge sort splits items into two groups, recursively sorts each group, and merges them into a final sorted sequence.
keyPoints.quote: A sort algorithm that splits the items to be sorted into two groups, recursively sorts each group, and merges them into a final, sorted sequence.

keyPoints.point: Merge sort recursively merges groups into a sorted sequence and its run time is Theta n log n.
keyPoints.quote: recursively sorts each group, and merges them into a final, sorted sequence. Run time is Θ(n log n).

keyPoints.point: Merge sort is an aggregate child that uses the divide and conquer approach as part of its design.
keyPoints.quote: Aggregate child (... is a part of or used in me.) divide and conquer.

keyPoints.point: Specializations of merge sort include balanced k-way merge sort and polyphase merge sort variants.
keyPoints.quote: Specialization (... is a kind of me.) k-way merge sort, balanced k-way merge sort, polyphase merge sort.

keyTerms.gloss: sort algorithm that can merge sorted groups together
keyTerms.quote: Specialization (... is a kind of me.) k-way merge sort, balanced k-way merge sort, polyphase merge sort.

keyTerms.gloss: amount of time used that grows as theta n log n
keyTerms.quote: Run time is Θ(n log n).

keyTerms.gloss: general strategy where a problem is divide and conquer by splitting into parts
keyTerms.quote: Aggregate child (... is a part of or used in me.) divide and conquer.

keyTerms.gloss: variant that can merge several sorted groups at once
keyTerms.quote: Specialization (... is a kind of me.) k-way merge sort, balanced k-way merge sort, polyphase merge sort.

keyTerms.gloss: procedure that splits items to be sorted into groups and sorts them
keyTerms.quote: A sort algorithm that splits the items to be sorted into two groups, recursively sorts each group, and merges them into a final, sorted sequence.
